main_body: A 4x3-tile (64x48) dark olive-green ground patch with a repeating tuft pattern. It is flat terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none. This is a flat ground surface seen from above, so there is no top and front split. The column scan shows a repeating 16-row cycle of an olive base (#404830) with 1-row tuft highlights (#677049, #515a3a) and dark specks (#262b1d).
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the standing-object 3/4 contract (top band plus front face) does not apply. The drawing is a seamless ground texture with no receding side faces and no elevation view of an object. It reads as a correct top-down ground fill for this kind.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours in total and a median of 8 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile, so the candidate is far thinner than the closest same-kind reference. It is only level with the paving reference (7). The tuft clumps repeat identically every 16 px, so the tiling is visible and mechanical, whereas the grass reference varies tile to tile. The ramp is about 5 steps (dark speck, base, mid, light, bright tuft), but the base olive covers most of the area and the accents are sparse single pixels. Texture dots are present, with no 5x5 flat fills (0%) and no black sticker outline (0% neutral dark pixels), but the density and variety fall clearly short of the grass bar.
